sections.content: How many people are "leisure and theme park attendants"?

17,455 people

were counted on the census as "leisure and theme park attendants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Leisure and theme park attendants monitor the operation of amusement arcades, check tickets of entry to theatres and cinemas and show people to their seats, operate rides at funfairs and theme parks, entertain and look after guests at holiday camps, and supervise museums and art galleries.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "leisure and theme park attendants" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "leisure and theme park attendants", 26.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "leisure and theme park attendants" was 60 to 64 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "leisure and theme park attendants" included:

  • sports and leisure assistants
  • bar staff
  • elementary sales occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "leisure and theme park attendants" there were a similar number of men and women (45.8% compared with 54.2%).

This means "leisure and theme park attendants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 45.8% and women made up 54.2% of "leisure and theme park attendants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "leisure and theme park attendants" included:

  • buyers and procurement officers
  • business and related research professionals
  • estate agents and auctioneers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "leisure and theme park attendants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "leisure and theme park attendants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "leisure and theme park attendants", 15.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (67.9% compared with 32.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93%) than self-employed (7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
